s: Im Grunde hast du ja recht — ganz recht — aber es war doch nur meine große Liebe zu dir — die stete Angst, die deine zu verlieren, […]
stet.et: Middle High German stæte, Old High German stāti, ultimately from the root of stehen (“to stand”). Cognate with Bavarian stad.

s: steady, continuous (without break, cessation, or interruption in time)
stetig.et: From Middle High German stætec (“firm, constant, stable”), Old High German stāti; analyzable as stet + -ig.

s: always; constantly; the whole time (very often)
every time (whenever some precondition is given)
stets.et: From Middle High German stetes, from Proto-Germanic *stēdi-; cognate with Dutch steeds. Synchronically analyzed as an adverbial formation stet (“steady, constant”) + -s; see there for more.

但与此相对的，是现代官员阶层的发展：它发展成为一支经过长期预备教育、受过专业训练、高度合格的脑力劳动者队伍，并且为了廉洁而发展出高度的等级荣誉；没有这种荣誉，可怕的腐败和庸俗市侩作风的危险就会作为命运笼罩在我们头上，也会威胁国家机器纯技术上的运作——而国家机器对经济的意义一直在稳步增长，并且还会继续增长，尤其是随着社会化的推进。
